A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors, title and substantial retained content. All 24 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v4 support comparison of text, equations, figures and references. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Figure 7 reports the survey's keyword-based analysis of annual arXiv publication counts and their growth. This qualifies as original descriptive data analysis, although model-performance findings are attributed to cited studies.

after.justification: Figure 8 retains and updates the publication-count analysis. These descriptive results qualify independently of the model-performance findings summarized from other studies.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes its own diffusion model or algorithm. V4 substantially expands descriptions of cited methods, without introducing a method component belonging to the survey itself.

E1.justification: The survey's publication analysis retains the same three keyword categories, Computer Science restriction and 2021–2025 coverage. Added application domains and benchmark mentions concern reviewed literature, not additional training or evaluation conducted by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a survey-proposed method. V1's Table I inventories inference techniques used by existing models; its removal is not removal of an experimental comparator set.

E3.justification: The publication-count captions specify the same keyword searches, Computer Science category and All fields search option. No revised collection or analysis procedure is documented. Newly described training settings belong to cited methods rather than changed experiments conducted by the survey.

E4.justification: V4 adds literature discussions of safety, quantization and long-context behavior, but no original ablation, robustness experiment or case study. Its new schedule plots illustrate mathematical functions rather than experimentally testing model sensitivity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests for its own analysis. Projected extensions already appear in v1's publication chart; v4 labels them explicitly. Discussions of variance reduction concern cited training methods.

E6.justification: The publication chart updates the 2025 counts and projections while retaining the increasing trend (v1 Figure 7; v4 Figure 8). V4 also adds attributed findings such as Seed Diffusion's 2146 tokens/s and omits v1's detailed LLaDA reversal-curse result discussion. These do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V4 adds the RDM routing recursion, a dedicated masked-diffusion formulation and loss derivation, TCSM objectives and their equivalence, and formal treatments of flexible-length generation, reinforcement learning and quantization. These substantially expand the mathematical account; block diffusion is retained and relocated. The new guidance Equation 108 also reverses the probability ratio used in Equation 35.

C1.justification: The comprehensive-survey contribution and up-to-10x acceleration claim remain. V4's introduction newly foregrounds superiority over autoregressive models on code generation, planning and Sudoku, and under data-constrained training with increased computation, modestly strengthening the stated performance case.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations of training on corrupted ground truth versus inference on model predictions, premature unmasking under strong guidance, temporal oscillation, diffusion-specific jailbreak vulnerabilities and accumulating quantization errors. It also removes v1's interpretation that successful prefilling indicates largely static visual perception. These materially expand and revise the discussion of mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: The linked literature collection changes from DLLM-Survey to Awesome-Discrete-Diffusion-LLM_MLLM. V4 also supplies concrete details for reviewed additions, such as Dream-Coder's 322B training tokens and Blockwise SFT's masking distribution. These are documentation and access-link changes, not evidence of rerunning existing experiments.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands the literature synthesis around flexible-length diffusion, code models, reinforcement learning, accelerated sampling, safety and quantization. The bibliography grows from 120 to 175 entries, with existing works retained after matching renumbering and bibliographic updates. The change extends the survey's research positioning beyond citation maintenance.

P1.justification: V4 shortens the abstract and introduction, combines LLaDA and LLaDA 1.5 into a series discussion, moves block diffusion into a new modeling section, and substantially condenses and reorganizes applications. Dedicated privacy/safety and quantization sections further change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V4 rebuilds the survey taxonomy in Figure 2, extends the timeline, adds information-flow panels to Figure 3 and introduces schedule plots in Figure 4. It removes v1's Table I and revises the publication chart's scale and legend. The unmasking, remasking and guidance diagrams are largely retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The dedicated masked-diffusion derivation and explanations of length control, alignment and diffusion-specific failure mechanisms make v4 more useful as a technical reference. However, removing Table I loses a compact comparison aid, and the new guidance Equation 108 conflicts with Equation 35's reverse-rate ratio. These drawbacks limit the net quality gain despite the substantial expansion.
